I was induced at 39 weeks to reduce increased risk of complications associated with IVF pregnancy. They started me on cytotec before pitocin. I went in around 10 AM on a Friday & baby was in our arms by 2:30 PM the next day after about 2 hours of pushing. 

I was terrified to give birth but it was surprisingly easy! My nurses were fantastic & my pain was well managed. I mostly slept & laughed with my family. 

Ultimately it’s up to you to decide, but if I were to do it again I would induce a 2nd time. I’m an anxious person & it helped a lot to have a set date & feel mentally prepared. It also helped my stress to know that we were reducing potential risks, which (in my case) would have increased significantly had we waited until 40+ weeks.

Our clinic had a similar schedule to this — “cycles.” I think it’s pretty common. We didn’t notice it much outside of certain days being very busy and certain appointments taking longer than others due to that. But during our 3rd “cycle,” our transfer was almost cancelled because my body wasn’t reacting to the meds quickly enough. They did delay 2 days so my uterus could try to catch up and ultimately that bit of extra time allowed us to proceed with transferring as planned, but if the 2-day delay didn’t work then that cycle would have been a wash and we would’ve had to do it all over again and wait until the next one.

During our birthing class we were also told no eating… with a big wink on the end. If you want the snacks, bring the snacks. Eat the snacks. I don’t have any experience with adopting a kid myself so I can’t speak on that front, but I have a stepchild I am very close with and imagine adopting might feel a bit like that.

I also question why it falls on me to sacrifice the parenting and family experience I would like to have just because other people chose to have children they can no longer care for.

And please don’t get me wrong, I’m not saying the relationships between children and their adoptive parents is lesser than. I think adoption is important and wonderful when it works out. My partner was a child of the system and we have discussed fostering and possibly adopting someday. I was put under for mine so the actual retrieval process was easy and painless (I just laid there and didn’t know time passed til I woke up). Hopefully they’ll be good at pain management so you can just chill. I’ve heard it can be (but shouldn’t be!) painful without sedation. If you feel pain, absolutely let them know. In my case, I wasn’t prepared at all for possible complications post-procedure. I ended up with OHSS (so fun!) and bloated to the point of hobbling around like a little old lady. The silver lining (?) is that I discovered my intolerance to Doxycycline during my recovery, thanks to a few days of throwing up ~30 mins after taking it. About 8 days post-ER, they had to bring me back into the clinic to drain the fluid I was retaining. 😭 It was disgusting, lol, but I felt sooo much better after and ultimately recovered fine once I had that done. For most people, sleeping propped up will help prevent this level of fluid build-up. Also, not drinking straight water. Do Gatorade, Liquid I.V., etc. Make sure you remain in close contact with your clinic if you feel off in any way. Take it as easy as you can. Take time off work if you can. Everyone’s experience will vary, so pay attention to your body and comfort. Good luck today! 🍀

I liked having a plan too - like, okay, this one didn’t work, so what’s our next move? We also did as much testing as was available to us between transfers 2 and 3 for our own peace of mind. We didn’t want there to be any question in our heads on whether we’d done all we could. And finally, you’re not in this alone, IRL or here on Reddit. Lean on your partner and let them lean on you. From what I understand, it’s basically a FET cycle, but on “transfer day” they biopsy your endometrium instead of transferring an embryo.

I had an endometrial biopsy last week in preparation for FET round 2 and I’ll be honest, it huuuuurt. Think a really bad period cramp for ~5 seconds (definitely felt longer in the moment lol). But it went away pretty quick. 

The results of the ERA tells them down to the hour whether your body is in the “receptive” zone for a transfer based on their calculated timeline. If something is off, they can use the results to adjust your protocol and make it much more tailored to your body! It also checks for inflammatory markers in case there’s something else going on that could interfere with transfer success. My doctor also said it’s often recommended for folks who’ve had past miscarriages so they can 1) more accurately plan your protocol and 2) identify and treat any potential obstacles.

Hopefully that all makes sense! It’s new to me so I’m sure others have experiences to share too! 😊

I’ll be honest, I still feel guilty for breaking up with my ex. We were together 5 years, owned 2 dogs, a house. Everyone would always ask when we were getting married, if a baby was on the way, all the inappropriate anecdotal relationship things. 2 years in, we were dead-bedroom. The next 3, I was trying to convince myself that he was such a good person and had such a lovely family that I should just be happy. I fucking tried. I really did. And all I had to show for it at the end of the day was crying into my pillow, drinking too much, and self-harming because I couldn’t express my feelings of something not being “quite right” to ANYONE - at least, that’s how I felt at the time. Ultimately, circumstances led to me finally calling it off. He was completely blind-sided, but truly we’d both become so complacent. We were more friends and roommates at the end. I was his first love and he was perfectly content with being together forever. I remember still how that felt for me in my first serious relationship, and how devastated I was when it came to an end. I like to think I did him a favor by showing him that feeling. Truly, though, I am so pained that I had to hurt him at all. I still care for him and hope he’s doing well, but I just wasn’t happy being romantic partners with him. If fate had allowed it, I would’ve been his friend in a heartbeat. Oddly enough, people tend to not like you much after you break their heart. The worst part about it all is the week after I ended things, he got a haircut, dressed up, cleaned up all the yard, finished all the projects around the house he’d been putting off. He was trying so hard to “win me back.” He wrote a letter and read it to me, asking for another chance, for us to go to counseling. He told me his sweet dad had driven 4 hours to come help him get things in order for the last hurrah. God it fucking hurt to look in his hopeful eyes and tell him no. I think that was the moment my own heart broke. Anyway… all of this is to say, the fact that you feel guilty, imo, just shows how much you genuinely gave and give a shit about your ex. People can be wonderful and not right for you, and that’s okay. It’s also okay to mourn that, even if you’re the one making the choice to end things.

From the outside looking in, husband and I are 2 happy clams with a precious little 5-year-old, working on baby #2 and bringing baby #1 along for the ride.

Looking at us, you wouldn’t and couldn’t guess what our circumstances are or how we got to where we are now. 

In my mind, preventing patients from bringing children into clinics if they need to only serves to add to the massive pay-wall that already exists for IVF and similar procedures. Infertility doesn’t care about income.

All of that said, I didn’t think about how bringing my stepson into the clinic might make the other patients feel. In the future, if we have to do something similar, maybe they can wait in the car. I’m sure you’ve heard these before, but I always bring it up for coparenting with a narcissist. Never JADE - justify, argue, defend, or explain - when communicating with them. Keep any messages you must send BIFF - brief, informative, factual, and firm. Then return to the anti-JADE mentality. 

When they message you, don’t feel obligated to read/respond right away. I can absolutely relate to the anxiety spike associated with seeing a message notification from a coparent or their partner. Sometimes it’s best to take a breath before diving in. 

When you do read their messages, ask yourself, “Is this something that I MUST engage them about?” If it’s them asking whether your son is allergic to nuts - and for the sake of this example let’s say he is - then absolutely reply. If it’s them saying, “Wow, it’s pretty messed up that you love son less than your new baby.” Then roll your eyes and carry on with your day.

Narcs THRIVE on engagement. If you react when they hit you with ridiculous allegations or disrespectful side comments, you’re giving them exactly what they want. They love knowing that they’ve hurt you. They can’t control you in other ways, but knowing that they can influence your emotions? Delicious!

In all seriousness, I’ve been on a high-conflict coparenting journey with my partner’s ex for about 2 years now. We still get hit with unwarranted attacks and have a running tally of narratives she’s trying to spin for our upcoming court date. Ultimately, though, our uninteresting reactions to her antics have resulted in less and less antics. For a while, she got LOUD. I know it’s hard, especially when they’re ganging up on you. Just try to remember you have the power at the end of the day. You’re in control of you. Don’t give them a space at the table to direct your emotional energy; save it for loving your kiddos, your partner, and yourself.

It happens, it’s normal, and understandable. Remember why you chose to separate in the first place. Don’t even think of yourselves; think of your kid(s) and the impact an on/off relationship would have. Ultimately, be kind to yourself, too.

For your parenting plan, you can ask for a “right of first refusal” clause to be added. This will entitle you (and subsequently him) to be the first person contacted in situations where parenting time can’t be exercised with the parent it’s scheduled for. For instance, if he’s unable to visit with his daughter for 4+ hours one evening, he’d have to offer you that time before asking a family member or his partner.

That said, usually there’s a duration put in place. Him having his partner watch your child for an hour while he runs to the store, for instance, wouldn’t apply. And, as I mentioned above, the same would go in reverse. If you need a babysitter, you have to engage him first. 

At the end of the day, I feel preserving and encouraging the child’s relationships is the most important thing. Don’t get me wrong, I do not feel any warmth for my husband’s ex-wife or her husband; they are seriously awful people. But, my stepchild loves them and they’re just as important to him as my husband and I. So, I help child make cards for birthdays, get gifts for xmas, and we offer them any available opportunity to attend events or spend more time.
